summary: Plausible, cleanly attributable single-row change: it removes a 1.5 us node from a single-kernel-dominated 13.2 us row worth 0.70%/us, and only the sliding verify_1 row plus an in-prepare interleaved gate decide it, so no companion is needed. The ~2 us estimate is optimistic. The real risks are the import/compile clock (this adds a 6th load_inline module on a base that was told not to gain one) and the multi-CTA new-key overwrite logic.
justification: Mechanism: FINDINGS profiles sliding verify_1 at 13.2 us shape = splitkv_attn_sk_kernel PSEUDO 9.9 us + _pre_attention_kernel 1.5 us. The floor is 0.1 us, so the row is entirely latency/launch-bound and deleting a graph node is the right kind of lever (LESSONS: on 5-15 us rows, deleting a node can matter more than kernel speed). Headline arithmetic checks out: the verify_1 load is about 46*13.2 + 16*30.3 = 1092 us, so -2 us x 46 is about -8.4% of that load, about +1.4% geomean over 6 loads. The expected shapes and directions match TASK weights: only sliding verify_1 moves, everything else is flat beyond the base. WEAKEST LINK: the '~1.8 us node gap' is shape-minus-kernel-sum, and that residual is not a clean gap measure. Single-kernel rows show similar residuals: sliding decode_1 12.1 vs 10.6 = 1.5 us with one kernel, sliding decode_16 15.5 vs 12.7 = 2.8 us, full decode_16 110.8 vs 110.3 = 0.5 us. So most of the 1.8 us likely stays after the fold. What reliably goes is the 1.5 us pre-attn kernel plus a fraction of a microsecond of inter-node gap, minus the in-kernel prologue on the critical path. At B=1 with ~256 tiles over ~132 CTAs (~2 tiles per CTA), nearly every CTA starts a segment and pays the q load + RMSNorm + RoPE before its first S MMA, and new-key CTAs also build K/V rows between cp_wait and the MMA. A realistic outcome is -0.8 to -1.8 us (+0.5 to +1.2% headline), still enough to clear a 1.03x gate (about 0.4 us). Precedent is mixed. The fold at full decode_1 alone was 22.4 -> 21.6 us within CI (full-decode1-sk-two-level-fused-preattn). V2 (fused pre alone) in combo-b1 was 0.883 of master. At B>=2 the fold was do-not-try (0.988x/1.014x), but there the kernel is 100-220 us; here it is 9.9 us. PRIOR: the cited prior is real and the difference is real (RoPE, 8 query tokens, 8 new rows read by many CTAs vs one owner-only row, sliding window). The prior field omits two related attempts. sliding-single-launch-fused-attention (Triton single-launch sliding with pre-attn folded; regression 0.945, lost verify_1) is a whole-design Triton rewrite and does not invalidate this targeted CUDA fold. fused-sliding-preattn-into-window-kernel (queued, hold) targeted the FA3/Triton window path. This is not on the do-not-try list: FUSED_PRE B>=2 is about full decode, and this differs in batch, layer and kernel scale. The new-key design departs from skF. In skF exactly one CTA reads the new row, so it is stored before the ring. Here new key m lies in pseudo-rows m..7, so up to 8 rows' tail tiles (possibly two tiles each when seq-8 straddles a 64-key boundary) are read by several CTAs, hence the smem overwrite. The design is sound only if every CTA overwrites every new-key position it loaded, identified by key index >= seq_b - 8 (not by slot), and the self-check asserts cache_loc[j] == page_table[0, seq-8+j] as _skf_case does.
confounders: merge-perkvhead-v3chain-sv32-tiled (the base, unmeasured, not landed): it moves full decode_1 (V3 chain) and sliding verify_32 (SV32 tiled), so the HEADLINE of this run mixes both changes. It does not touch the sliding verify_1 path (B=1 verify keeps master's pre-attn and PSEUDO route), so the sliding verify_1 row and the in-prepare PATH CHOSEN numbers stay attributable. Its separate run gives the base headline to difference against. It also adds a 5th load_inline module, which this change's 6th module compounds (see open questions).

restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn (landed the B=1 sliding verify PSEUDO route this change modifies): it is the incumbent, not a confounder of the gain, but its route/grid at B=1 is picked by a prepare-time selector. The FUSED gate must compare against master's routed variant/grid from the SAME run, as specified, and print every FUSED grid spec. Otherwise a grid-selection flip could pass for a fold gain.

fused-preattention-triton (the _pre_attention_kernel being folded): the numeric reference for the new cache rows. Triton sin/cos vs accurate sincosf differ in 1-6% of E4M3 bytes at large positions (~80000 * inv_freq rad here), so a byte-exact cache comparison would falsely fail. The hypothesis correctly uses rel L2 < 2e-2. No timing confound.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change has one routed effect, the sliding verify_1 row at B=1. No other landed hypothesis or base change touches that row's launch sequence, and the hypothesis prints an interleaved cold-L2 head-to-head of [FUSED PSEUDO] vs [pre-attn + master's routed PSEUDO] in prepare. A gain or a loss on that row is therefore readable from the row and the PATH CHOSEN line alone. An ab-revert of the base merge would only disentangle the headline, which the merge's own run already does. An ab-revert of the PSEUDO route is meaningless because the fold is defined on it. A 'q-only fold' control (fold q, keep a separate tiny K/V-store kernel) would split the prologue cost from the K/V-overwrite cost, but it re-adds a node, so a fused-vs-unfused difference would stay ambiguous. It is better done as in-prepare DIAG timings (FUSED with K/V build disabled on a correctness-irrelevant timing-only instantiation) than as a scored run.
rules_flags: Not a rules violation, but tighten the gate: per the 2026-10-25 lesson (single-round 1.02x selectors mis-routed bf16), require two interleaved rounds both >= 1.03x with candidate IQR <= 1.5x the incumbent's before routing B=1 to FUSED. A single round at 1.03x on a 13 us row is about a 0.4 us call.

The new-key owner must come from the in-kernel tile partition formula (as skF's tile_owner), never from data-dependent host control flow at kernel_fn time. The host owner check is prepare-only validation on synthetic lens, and the routing predicate stays config-only (sliding, window 2048, q_len 8, B == 1, page 1, tp8).

Concurrent global store (owner) and cp.async reads (other CTAs) of the same 8 cache slots is a deliberate benign race only if EVERY reader overwrites EVERY new-key position in smem before use. Any missed position (tile-boundary straddle, partial tiles when lens < 8, the window lower bound) makes the output depend on stale or torn bytes that the self-check may not catch with coherent data. The self-check should also run with the target slots pre-filled with NaN/garbage bytes, not just 'other rows unchanged'.

Run time: this is a 6th load_inline module on a base that already raises the import clock to 5 modules (222 s across 4 on master) inside a 15-minute run that includes compile. A timeout is charged as a run. Give the new module its own deadline and skip-to-fallback (PATH CHOSEN) if the import clock is past a fixed budget before building it.
open_questions: Import budget: with merge-perkvhead-v3chain-sv32-tiled already at 5 modules, could FUSED PSEUDO be built inside an existing module, or shared with the queued sliding-decode-sk-s3-fused-preattn-rope (TOK=1), so the two sliding folds do not each add a module? At minimum, what is the deadline at which muse_sv1_fused_v1 is skipped?

Does the raw bf16 K/V source for the 8 new rows (8 tokens x 2 kv heads x 64 x (k,v), ~4 KB) get prefetched in the prologue cp.async group, or loaded at the overwrite point between cp_wait and the S MMA? The latter puts a global-load latency on the critical path of every new-key CTA.

Is the ~1.8 us 'node gap' real? Single-kernel rows show 0.5-2.8 us shape-minus-kernel residuals, so the realistic gain may be nearer -1 us. Print the gate's unfused and FUSED medians so the expected-vs-measured gap can be booked either way.

The new-key positions are identified by key index >= seq_b - 8. Does the self-check include a len where seq-8 straddles a 64-key tile boundary and the window-start edge cases (lens 2047/2048/2055 are listed; add a len with (seq-8) % 64 == 60)?

Is the 5.473 q scale (and the e4m3 cast of q at the same point as _pre_attention_kernel) reproduced exactly, and are k_scale/v_scale handled for the kv_scale 0.015625 test (the B=1 route is config-gated to page 1, which no B=1 q_len 8 test hits, so only the self-check covers it)?
